MINUTES
  REGULAR MEETING
  GLENDALE TRANSPORTATION & PARKING COMMISSION
  APRIL 22, 2019

  DATE:  Monday, April 22, 2019
  TIME:  6:00 p.m.
  LOCATION:  City Council Chambers
  613 East Broadway, Glendale CA 91206

The regular meeting of the Glendale Transportation and Parking Commission (TPC) of Monday,
April 22, 2019 was called to order at 6:00 p.m.
Commissioner Yacoubian motioned to sit in as Chair Pro Tem for Chairperson Kurkjian because
the Chair was feeling ill.

1. REGULAR BUSINESS AGENDA- 6:00 Chair Pro Tem Yacoubian called the meeting to
order.
  a. Roll Call- Yacoubian, Gonzalez, Kurkjian, Nazarian
  Absent: Sahakian
  b. Flag Salute – Chair Pro Tem Yacoubian

2. POSTING OF AGENDA
  The agenda for the Monday, April 22, 2019 Regular Meeting of the Glendale
  Transportation & Parking Commission was posted by Thursday, April 18, 2019 before
  5:00 p.m. on the bulletin board outside of City Hall.

3. ACTION
  a. Installation of Speed Humps on Lomita Avenue between Glendale Avenue and
  Louise Street

Assistant Director for the Public Works Department, Edward Hitti, introduced the acting Principal
Traffic Engineer, Pastor Casanova, who presented this item to the Commission. Mr. Casanova
mentioned the request of local residents as well as the staff at the neighboring school, Holly
Family Grade School, to place speed humps on Lomita Avenue. The residents and school staff
expressed concerns about habitual speeding by vehicles traveling down Lomita Avenue
between Glendale Avenue and Louise Street. In his presentation, Mr. Casanova explained that
the engineering assessment of Lomita Avenue showed that the street’s conditions met the
speed and volume criteria to implement the speed humps and that traffic calming measures are
allowable for the following reasons: Lomita Street is a local street, is located in a residential
area, is in a school zone and is not on a Fire Response Route. Mr. Casanova collected a
petition from Holy Family School representatives, signed by 30 out the 34 residents on the
block, rendering 88% show of support. Staff recommends that two speed humps be installed on
Lomita Avenue between Glendale Avenue and Louise Street.

Chair Pro Tem Yacoubian raised some concerns regarding emergency response routes, as well
as a potential domino effect if drivers are deferred from Lomita Avenue onto other streets
causing speeding in other areas. She asked if there was any indication of who the speeders are,
if they are parents of children who attend Holy Family, or if they are just passing residents. She
also asked if staff from Holy Family School had reached out to parents to try and slow traffic
down during pick up and drop off times.
 Mr. Casanova acknowledged all of Chair Pro Tem Yacoubian’s concerns and addressed each
accordingly. He looked into the local emergency response routes and confirmed that the
nearest emergency response route is on Louise Street and would not be affected by speed
humps on Lomita Avenue. He also mentioned that since the main concern is people speeding
down Lomita Avenue, rather than a large volume of traffic, there is not a concern of a domino
effect of excess traffic on neighboring streets, such as Elk Avenue. According to the traffic
counts conducted by his team during school hours, Mr. Casanova mentioned studies that
showed the traffic and speeders were a mixture of parents of the school children attending Holy
Family and also passing residents. Mr. Casanova mentioned that he was not aware if the
school had done any public outreach in attempts to slow traffic.

Chair Pro Tem Yacoubian expressed her concern regarding a lack of alternative measures that
she felt should have taken place before requesting to install speed humps, such as striping or
placing a large mobile sign to warn drivers of the local speed limit. Mr. Hitti stepped in and
explained that those measures have been taken in the past and have proven to not be affective
unless there is a police officer to enforce the speed limits, or a physical barrier to really slow
down traffic.

Chairperson Kurkjian suggested to install one speed hump, instead of two, due to the low
volume of vehicles. Mr. Casanova explained that there is a minimum and maximum length to
space out each speed hump and installing one speed hump would exceed the maximum
distance allowed. Mr. Hitti added that if one speed hump does not slow down traffic, the City
will spend roughly twice the amount as the original plans to install two. Chairperson Kurkjian
mentioned his concern of inundating south Glendale with speed humps. Mr. Casanova
acknowledged this concern and informed the Commission that there are always less permanent
measures that can be implemented before the installation of speed humps.

Moved: Gonzalez  Seconded: Nazarian
Roll Call: Gonzalez, Yacoubian, Kurkjian, Nazarian
Absent: Sahakian

  a. March 4, 2019, Special Meeting

  b. March 25, 2019, Special Meeting

5. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  Discussion is limited to items NOT a part of this agenda. Each speaker is allowed five
  minutes. The Commission may question the speaker but there will be no debate or
  decision.
 6. COMMISSION/STAFF COMMENTS

Mr. Hitti introduced the new Director of Public Works, Mr. Yazdan Emrani.

Mr. Casanova proceeded to give an update regarding the double right turn lane which leads to
the southbound on-ramp for the 2-freeway from Mountain Street. Since the initial request to
take down the “no right turn on red” sign from this intersection had been made, Mr. Casanova
had met with Caltrans for a field study and had found the best solution was to place a blank out
“no right turn on red” LED sign which would be triggered only once there was traffic traveling
westbound on Mountain attempting to make a left southbound turn onto the 2-freeway. Mr. Hitti
mentioned that Caltrans would not be funding this project, but would be involved in the design
aspect of the project and would be issuing encroachment permits in order for the City to
complete the work. The project would be expected to be completed in six months to one year.
Mr. Casanova also spoke with Caltrans about the signal timing issue of the northbound off-ramp
from the 2-freeway which would cause vehicles making a left westbound turn onto Mountain
Street to get caught on a red light, thus causing severe traffic build up. During the same field
study, Caltrans was able to adjust the timing on the spot and relieve the traffic coming from the
off-ramp.

Commissioner Nazarian expressed his confusion about the 2-freeway off-ramp going from the
northbound 2-freeway onto westbound Mountain Street. He mentioned there are three lanes,
but it is not clear which lanes are designated left turn lanes. He recommended striping to
distinguish which lanes allow drivers to turn left onto Mountain Street. Chair Pro Tem seconded
that concern. Mr. Casanova said he would make that request of Caltrans since the location in
question falls in their purview of maintenance.

Chair Pro Tem Yacoubian asked Mr. Hitti for some insight to the recent passing of AB1069
regarding taxi cab company rules and restrictions and what Glendale plans to do to implement
these new guidelines. Mr. Hitti explained that the City has already been approached by taxi cab
companies requesting to put their permits on hold, or perhaps allow them to operate on expired
permits, until the City solidifies their new guidelines. Mr. Hitti explained that the taxi cab
companies were instructed to operate as usual, renewing their permits, until staff has the
opportunity to go to Council for adoption of the new ordinance.

7. ADJOURNMENT: 7:10 p.m.

Moved: Kurkjian  Second: Gonzalez
